newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus to issue eurobonds this year - deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Belarus to issue eurobonds this year - deputy PM.

text.p: Belarus is going ahead with plans to issue a Eurobond in 1997 and plans to sign a memorandum with the World Bank soon, first Deputy Prime Minister Pyotr Prokopovich told a news conference on Thursday.

"The finance ministry and the central bank have started work on issuing Eurobonds. We hope to get results from the paper, which will be issued on European markets, this year," said Propokovich, who also heads a government securities commission.
He said the issue volume had not been set, adding: "First our paper must be recognised on the European market".
Minsk would need an international credit rating before tapping financial markets and most investors would seek clear evidence of a credible economic reform programme.

Christopher Willoughby of the World Bank's Minsk office said this week that signing a memorandum with the bank agreeing to liberalise prices and the currency market by July 1 would help Belarus's quest to raise cash in Europe.
Prokopovich said: "The memorandum will be signed in April or May. We will fulfil the conditions in it, but want them to be realistic."
He also promised Belarus would immediately repay $20 million owed from an expired Hermes credit line from budget funds.
The World Bank, which has lent $170 million to Belarus, is prepared to issue a credit of $40 million to support private business with increases to follow -- if it accepts its conditions.
The International Monetary Fund has suspended its loan programme to Belarus until President Alexander Lukashenko initiates effective reforms.
